τῆς εἰς αὐτὸν πίστεως καὶ τῆς ἐξ αὐτοῦ δυνάμεως οὐδὲν οὐδεὶς δύναται ποιῆσαι, ἣν
ὁ πατὴρ οὐ γεωργεῖ ὡς μὴ χρῄζουσαν ἐπιμελείας, ἀλλὰ τὰ κλήματα. κλήματα δέ
εἰσιν τοῦ Χριστοῦ ὡς ἑνωθέντες αὐτῷ οἱ πιστοὶ διὰ τῆς ἐνοικήσεως τοῦ ἁγίου
πνεύματος καὶ γεγονότες «θείας φύσεως κοινωνοί», οἳ καὶ ἐπιμελείας τυγχάνουσι
παρὰ τοῦ πατρός. ὁ δὲ Χριστὸς ὡς ῥίζα συνέχει τοὺς πιστοὺς καὶ ζωογονεῖ διὰ τοῦ
ἁγίου πνεύματος· οὐ γὰρ ἀφ' ἑνὸς γέγονε προσώπου ἡ σωτηρία, ἀλλ' ἀπὸ τῆς θείας
τριάδος. 510 {3Jο 15, 2}3Ὁ πιστὸς κλῆμά ἐστι τῆς νοητῆς ἀμπέλου, ὅς ἐστι Χριστὸς
καὶ οὐδὲν ὠφελεῖται ἐκ μόνης πίστεως, ἀλλὰ χρεία καὶ ἐναρέτων ἔργων ἅπερ
γίνεται διὰ καθαρμῶν. 511 {3Jο 15, 2}3Οἱ κολλώμενοι «τῷ κυρίῳ» καὶ μὴ ἀξίως
αὐτοῦ πολιτευόμενοι κολάζονται, οἱ δὲ εὐσεβεῖς ζῶντες πολὺν φέρουσι τὸν καρπόν.
ἐὰν πίστιν ἔχωμεν, ἔργα δὲ μὴ ἔχωμεν, ὡς νεκρὰ καὶ ἄκαρπα κλήματα ἐκβάλλει

κόπτων. ἤτοι κλήματα ἄκαρπά εἰσιν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι. 512 {3Jο 15, 2 3}3Ταῦτα λέγει περὶ
ὧν ἔμελλον ὑπομένειν πειρασμῶν, οἵτινες αὐτοὺς ἐποίουν δοκιμωτέρους. οἱ
εὐσεβῶς ζῶντες πολὺν φέρουσι καρπόν. 513 {3Jο 15, 4}3Κἂν ἑνωθῇ τις Χριστῷ διὰ
τοῦ ἐν πνεύματι ἁγιασμοῦ, ἀλλὰ χρῄζει καὶ τῆς τελείας ἀγάπης ἔχεσθαι καὶ
ἀκολουθεῖν αὐτῷ· ὁ γὰρ ἀποκοπεὶς ἀπὸ Χριστοῦ διὰ τὸ μὴ ἔχειν τέλειον τὸν
ἁγιασμὸν καὶ τὴν ἀγάπην, οὐ δύναταί τι ποιῆσαι ἀγαθόν. 514 {3Jο 15, 4}3∆ιὰ τὸ μὴ
δύνασθαι καρποφορεῖν εἰ μὴ μόνους τοὺς προσηλωμένους αὐτῷ καλεῖ ἑαυτὸν
ἄμπελον ὡς ἐξ αὐτοῦ δυναμουμένους. 515 {3Jο 15, 5}3Καὶ αὐτὸς οὐχ ἥττων τοῦ

τὸν θεόν· οὐ γὰρ βιάζεται ἡμῶν τὸ αὐτεξούσιον. 5 {3Jο 15, 10}3Οὐ γὰρ μόνον δεῖ

πιστεύειν, ἀλλὰ καὶ ποιεῖν τὰς ἐντολάς. 521 {3Jο 15, 12 13}3Ὡς διδάσκαλος τῆς
οἰκουμένης παραδίδωσιν αὐτοῖς ταῦτα ὁ Χριστός, ὅτι ἡ ἀγάπη κεφάλαιόν ἐστι τῶν
ἀρετῶν, ἡ ἐντολὴ αὐτοῦ τὸ ὑπεραποθνῄσκειν τῶν φίλων καὶ τὸ ὑπὲρ ἑαυτοὺς
ἀγαπᾶν τοὺς φίλους. 522 {3Jο 15, 13}3∆είκνυσιν, ὅτι ἡ ἀναχώρησις αὐτοῦ οὐκ ἦν
μίσους, ἀλλ' ἀγάπης· ὑπὲρ γὰρ ὑμῶν ἀποθνῄσκω. 523 {3Jο 15, 14}3∆ιὰ τὴν ἀρετὴν τὸ
τῶν δούλων ὑπερβάντες μέτρον γεγόνασι φίλοι. ἀνακομίζει δὲ τοὺς δούλους ἐπὶ τὴν
ὑπὲρ φύσιν δόξαν, ἐὰν ἑκουσίως ποιῶσι τὰ τῷ θεῷ ἀρεστά. 524 {3Jο 15, 15}3Ἀντὶ τοῦ
ὅσα ἐχρῆν ἀκοῦσαι αὐτούς· ὃ δὲ λέγει αἰνιγματωδῶς, τοῦτό ἐστιν, ὅτι οὐχ ὡς
pass_a_gloss: trust in him and power from him, nobody can do anything. The Father does not tend a root that needs no care, but the shoots. Christ's shoots are the faithful joined by Spirit dwelling and made sharers of divine nature, and the Father tends them. As root Christ holds and enlivens believers through the Spirit; salvation rose from the Trinity, not one person alone. A believer is a shoot of the mind vine, Christ, and faith alone helps nothing; virtuous deeds through cleansings are also needed. Those stuck to the Lord yet living unworthy of him are punished; the devout bear much fruit. Faith without works are dead barren shoots he cuts away. Or barren shoots are the Judeans. He speaks of coming trials that will prove them. The devout bear much fruit. Even Spirit union needs holding perfect love and following him; cut off for lacking perfect holiness and love, one can do no good. Since only those fixed to him can bear fruit, he names himself vine as the source of their power. He himself, not less than the Father, shares in caring for the disciples. That is: the Father rejoices when you stay in me. Your deeds praise the Father. Serving God spiritually and skipping the letter makes Christ's disciples and much fruit. Loving God is in our power; he does not coerce free will. Believe and also keep the commands. As teacher of the world Christ hands them this: love crowns the virtues; his command is dying for friends and loving friends more than self. Departure was love, not hate; I die for you. Virtue lifted them past slave measure into friendship. He raises slaves to glory beyond nature when they freely please God. Meaning: as much as they needed to hear; and the riddle is that not as
pass_b_english: faith into him and the power from him no one can do anything—which the Father does not cultivate as needing no care, but the branches. And branches of Christ are the faithful united to him through the Holy Spirit’s indwelling and become “partakers of the divine nature” (2 Peter 1:4), who also receive care from the Father. And Christ as root holds the faithful together and makes them alive through the Holy Spirit; for salvation did not come from one person but from the divine Trinity.
The believer is a branch of the intelligible vine, which is Christ, and gains nothing from faith alone, but there is need also of virtuous works which come through cleansings.

Those who cling “to the Lord” and do not live worthily of him are punished, but the pious living bear much fruit. If we have faith but not works, he casts out as dead and fruitless branches, cutting. Or fruitless branches are the Jews.
He says these things about the trials they were going to endure, which made them more proven. Those living piously bear much fruit.

Even if someone is united to Christ through sanctification in the Spirit, still he needs also to hold to perfect love and follow him; for the one cut off from Christ through not having perfect sanctification and love cannot do any good.
Because fruit-bearing is impossible except for those fixed to him alone, he calls himself vine as ones empowered from him.
And he himself, not less than the Father, contributes to the disciples’ care.
That is: the Father rejoices when you remain in me. Through what you do the Father is praised.
This makes Christ’s disciples and bears much fruit: serving God spiritually, passing by the letter.
It is in us to love God; for he does not force our free will.
For one must not only believe but also do the commandments.
As teacher of the inhabited world Christ hands these things to them: that love is the sum of the virtues, his commandment is to die for friends and to love friends more than yourselves.
He shows that his departure was not of hatred but of love; for I die for you.
Through virtue, having surpassed the measure of slaves, they became friends. And he raises slaves up to glory beyond nature if they willingly do what is pleasing to God.
That is: as much as they needed to hear; and what he says enigmatically is this: that not as
